claims.reason: waitForExit and stopChild accept exit before the normal stdio close boundary, and the per-descriptor tail is released after readline.close without retaining the child for that normal unsettled path.
The child exit handler rejects the operation immediately, so a valid final identified stdout result that has not yet reached readline can be discarded by the completed guard.

The timeout is an explicit bounded recovery boundary followed by app.relaunch for Restart and app.exit in finally; the report does not show the old process continuing after exit to create an actionable concurrent mutation.
main.cjs discards browserHost.destroy errors before awaiting browserControl.close, allowing the cleanup callback to resolve and recovery to report cleaned true after partial browser-host teardown.
Duplicate of review1 claim 1: the same normal exit-before-close ownership gap remains in waitForExit, stopChild, and descriptor scope release.

roots.title: Helper ownership is released before normal stdio close settlement
roots.trigger: A helper emits process exit while one of its stdio streams has not yet reached the close boundary; waitForExit or the already-exited fast path returns and the descriptor operation scope is released.
roots.fix: Track exit and stdio close independently, retain the exact child until close is observed or a surfaced bounded failure occurs, and release the descriptor scope only after settlement.

roots.title: Final helper response can lose to immediate exit rejection
roots.trigger: The helper writes a valid identified result and exits before readline delivers the buffered stdout line; the exit listener rejects first and completed suppresses the result.
roots.fix: Defer exit failure until the stdout protocol and close boundary have been consumed, allowing a valid identified result or helper error to decide the operation first.

roots.title: Startup recovery hides partial browser-host cleanup failure
roots.trigger: BrowserHost.destroy throws during startup recovery while the later browser control close succeeds; the caller's empty catch lets the cleanup callback resolve successfully.
roots.fix: Continue independent cleanup, retain the first browser-host cleanup error, and return a failed cleanup result with bounded detail so recovery cannot report cleaned true after partial teardown.
